working_candidate.selected_as: working scene-05 output candidate for the current video
working_candidate.important: This PNG is a WORKING CANDIDATE ONLY. It is NOT added to product-lock, NOT used as a reference/source for any future generation (this scene or any other), and NOT treated as accepted -- candidate_status in its own QA report remains pending_manual_review. Reference policy is unchanged: only real-product-v1 product photos under product-lock/real-v1 (product/handles/bottom) are ever allowed as image references.

owner_decision: Stop the C1/C2/C3 local deterministic compositing path for scene-05 (generated AI air fryer/basket/kitchen plates + real-product-v1 pasted on top via APPROVED_TRANSFORM_B or a per-plate rigid transform fallback). Every attempt in this path produced visible seams/artifacts or misalignment. New direction: PRODUCT ONLY MEANS PRODUCT ONLY -- see campaign_visual_policy.json (mandatory_product_reference, forbidden_global_reference_categories) and scene-05-product-reference-only-dry-run.json for the replacement approach.

C1.approach: product_placement_plate: AI draws kitchen/hands/basket/food plate (frontal basket, level left/right hand tabs), real-product-v1 pasted on top via fixed APPROVED_TRANSFORM_B.
C1.detail: AI plate drew its own black liner/tray-like insert in the basket (a duplicate of the product itself); separately, APPROVED_TRANSFORM_B (calibrated against a fixed reference photo) landed the real product outside this plate's actual basket location entirely.

C2.approach: Same product_placement_plate approach, revised prompt: high 3/4 top-down camera, diagonal upper-left-to-lower-right axis, asymmetric hand heights matching product_45deg's own photographed angle, plus a rigid per-plate transform fallback.
C2.detail: Camera angle and hand asymmetry direction were correct this time, and no duplicate product was drawn, but hands still landed ~150-160px from the real handle tabs even with the best achievable rigid-transform fit (an occlusion-compositing problem: correct front/back occlusion around a hand gripping a handle tab cannot be solved by a global rigid transform).

C3.approach: Same product_placement_plate approach, no-hands result shot: AI draws kitchen/basket/food only (no hands/person at all), real-product-v1 pasted on top via a per-plate rigid transform fallback (99.3% basket-opening footprint fit achieved).
C3.detail: Best geometric fit of the three attempts (no duplicate product, no hands to misalign, 99.3% footprint match) -- but the real-product-v1 layer still visibly reads as pasted onto the AI plate: a hard seam and a background-bleed-through artifact from the product photo's own source image are visible on close inspection. Local deterministic pixel-compositing of a real photo onto a fresh AI plate keeps producing this class of defect regardless of transform accuracy.
C3.important: C3's output PNGs (scene-05-c3-*.png) are diagnostic evidence of why this approach was rejected -- NOT a reference asset, NOT a locked background, NOT to be reused in any future generation or video.

product_reference_only_v1.approach: PRODUCT ONLY MEANS PRODUCT ONLY, mode=edit with ONE real-product-v1 photo (product_45deg_master) as the sole image reference, everything else (kitchen/basket/food) described in text -- no deterministic pixel compositing at all.
product_reference_only_v1.detail: No compositing seams (structural advantage over C1/C2/C3): the whole frame is a single coherent AI generation guided by the reference. Flat corner handle tab + horizontal slot correctly reproduced on one side, ribbed-bottom pattern visible, exactly 3 chicken thighs + potato wedges, no hands/person, clean basket. Superseded by v1 -> v2 after review (see product_reference_only_v2 below).
product_reference_only_v1.important: scene-05-product-reference-only-candidate.png is a CANDIDATE ONLY -- never promoted to reference, never added to product-lock.

product_reference_only_v2.approach: Same mode=edit approach, FOUR real-product-v1 photos as references (product_45deg_master, product_top_master, both_handles_master, bottom_loop_master) instead of one -- more geometric coverage of the product for the model to draw from.
product_reference_only_v2.detail: Improved over v1: BOTH flat corner handle tabs with horizontal-slot geometry now correctly reproduced (v1 only clearly showed one). Ribbed bottom visible. No compositing seams. Note: sha256 check found both_handles_master.png byte-identical to product_45deg_master.png (pre-existing asset-pack characteristic, same crop_coordinates/source photo) -- so 3 visually distinct images were actually sent, not 4.
product_reference_only_v2.important: scene-05-product-reference-only-v2-candidate.png is the SELECTED WORKING CANDIDATE for the current video (see working_candidate above) -- still NOT a reference, NOT in product-lock, NOT a source for future generations.

conclusions_kept.note: C3's decision to drop hands/lifting from the scene concept remains correct -- the failure was in the pixel-compositing mechanism (pasting a real photo onto an AI plate produces seams no matter how well the transform is tuned), not in the no-hands scene concept itself.
